sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Banisteriopsis caapi is a woody climbing vine native to tropical South America, especially Amazonian forests. It bears opposite leaves about 8–18 × 3.5–8 cm, small pink flowers around 12–14 mm and winged samara fruits. Flowering and fruiting are reported as uncommon in some accounts.

sections.title: Chemistry and safety
sections.text: The vine contains psychoactive beta-carboline alkaloids. Ayahuasca is a brewed preparation made from this vine and often other plants; the name does not refer simply to the plant. It can interact dangerously with medicines and other substances. No ingestion, recipe or self-treatment is recommended. The plate's climbing stems, opposite leaves and pink flowers fit the species.
